course_description:
This course will introduce students to the history, sources, principal legal concepts, institutions, and methodology of the common law in Australia. The course will provide students whose backgrounds are not in the common law with a sound basis for further study in a common law system.

This course is designed to give an overview of the fundamental structure, institutions and traditions of the common law, to enable students to undertake other courses which presume a knowledge of the common law. In this way students will be equipped to successfully complete other courses in the Master's programs and to study specific areas of Australian law.

Thus, this course covers key features of the Australian legal system. It identifies the sources of Australian law, theﾠinstitutional settings in which the law operates, and the methodology and jurisprudence of common law. Case analysis and statutory interpretation in aﾠcommon law context are included as well as an overview of the adversarial approach to litigation. In addition to the substance of the Australian legal system, students will be introduced to the legal research skills necessary to successfully complete other courses in the Masters programs.

course_aims:
Education Mission Statement

The mission of the School of Law is to educate you in and about the law. We seek to assist you to think critically about the law and to investigate its structures, principles, policies, and values. This is achieved by engaging with you as fellow investigators in a range of critical and intellectual conversations about the law and its place in society. Our role is thus to guide you in your own intellectual journey in the law and to equip you with the necessary skills that will enable you to continue that journey long after you have left the School.

Course Aims

This course is designed for those with no formal knowledge of the Australian legal system.ﾠ It aims to introduce key features of the law such as: sources, terminology, presumptions, institutions, methodologies and application, with emphasis on the role of case law and statutory law within the Australian legal system.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the Common Law system of justice and the main ways in which it differs from other legal systems.
Understand the way in which the Australian legal system operates.
Articulate the role of case law and statutory law in the Australian legal system.
Demonstrate knowledge of the legal institutions within which the Australian legal system operates.
Effectively and efficiently locate both print and electronic sources of law.
Communicate effectively and professionally, using writing styles which reflect the conventions of academic and legal expression and organisation.

assessment_details.title: Research Plan
assessment_details.task_description: Outline in one page (which you will be given in class) how you would conduct research for a law essay. The topic for the proposed essay will be given to you in class. A research plan is the first step before writing a proposal (which is longer and more detailed) and then the subsequent research essay. Your plan is the blueprint for how you will conduct your research and approach the topic. It sets out your initial thoughts logically and concisely. Key components: Research question Either sub-questions, or, the steps you will take to answer the research question. Methodology: identify how you will conduct your research (comparative, quantitative, case law, doctrinal analysis). Sources: Identify how you will locate the sources with a brief note as to their importance. AI: if you will use AI what question or questions (the prompts) would you ask? Reflection: are there any challenges to this research, or, its significance. There will be examples of plans given to you in seminar 2 prior to completing this in-class task. Students will have 10 minutes of perusal time and 1 hour of writing time to answer the case analysis question based on the legal reasoning of a hypothetical case provided. learning_activities.topic: Session 2 Legal writing, communication and comprehension UQ College to conduct a practical writing task. Learning outcomes: L06
Session 3 Legal Writing Skills I Research Plans and Proposals. How to design a research plan and how this differs from a proposal. Plagiarism and use of AI. Learning outcomes: L06
Session 4 Australian Legal and Political System and the Constitution The Australian Legal and Political System and Constitutional Framework. Learning outcomes: L01, L04

Session 5 Library Research Workshop Starting legal research: Primary and Secondary Resources. How to search for cases, statutes and secondary materials. Introduction to the law library and an overview of the basics of legal research. Learning outcomes: L05
Session 6 Development of the Common Law The Development of the Common Law in England and subsequently in Australia. Learning outcomes: L01, L04

Session 7 Australian Courts of Law Australian Courts of Law: court hierarchy in Australia and the operation of stare decisis. Key institutions: judiciary, legal practitioners, DPP. Learning outcomes: L01, L04
The Research Plan In this session students will complete a short one-page research plan. Learning outcomes: L06
Session 8 International Law International Law in the Common Law Method. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Session 9 Case Law Operation of Case Law & Precedents. Case Studies: Terra Nullius to Mabo and Beyond. In this seminar, there will also be a practice quiz. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

Session 10 Comparative analysis Comparing the role of the courts, case law and methods of citation. Two streams. The stream for Chinese students is taken by Dr Wenting Chen. The stream for other students is taken by Professor Ann Black In this seminar, the first quiz will be held. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L06
Session 11 Legislation in the common law system How is legislation made (enacted) and its role in the common law method. How to access legislation and how to read it. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L06
Session 12 Statutory Interpretation in the Common Law Method How legislation is interpreted - the common law approach. In this seminar, the second quiz will be held. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Session 13 Legal Writing Skills II In class-problem solving exercises using legislation (Queensland Criminal Code) and cases. Introducing the IRAC method. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L06

Session 14 The Criminal Trial The Criminal Trial: Australian criminal proceedings. Features of an adversarial system. Mock trial in the Moot Court (depending on class size). Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Session 15 Comparative Analysis: Adversarial v Inquisitorial Comparative Analysis: Adversarial v Inquisitorial. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04
Session 16 Equity: origin, role, and contemporary significance Equity: origin and role. How equity complements the common law. The third quiz will be held in this seminar. Learning outcomes: L01, L06
Session 17 Legal Writing Skills III The assignment - discussion on an evaluative essay: structure, argument, sources and referencing. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06
Session 18 Overview, consultation and discussion In-semester Exam - Case analysis (30%). Overview, consultation, questions and discussion. Learning outcomes: L01, L06
